problem: Language-guided embodied benchmarks such as ALFRED allow only one-way communication: the agent receives an instruction and cannot ask for clarification. ALFRED also has only 7 goal types and 8 near-deterministic sub-goal types. Because of this, models can reach SOTA by classifying the task type from the high-level instruction alone, without really following instructions.
motivation: Humans ask questions when instructions are ambiguous or incomplete, for example 'pick up the knife' when two knives are present. Embodied agents that can ask targeted questions and use the answers should resolve ambiguity and recover from failure better. Prior dialogue benchmarks (CVDN, TEACh) predict actions from a dialogue history rather than having the agent actively ask clarification questions. Prior ask-for-help work covers navigation only, not long-horizon manipulation with irreversible state changes.
key_idea: Augment ALFRED into DialFRED, a benchmark with 25 sub-goal task types, deliberately under-specified instructions, 53K human-annotated QAs and a ground-truth-state oracle. The paper then provides a questioner-performer baseline: an LSTM questioner, pre-trained on human question choices and RL-fine-tuned, decides when and what to ask; an Episodic Transformer performer acts on the instruction plus the QAs.
insight: Adding QAs helps a lot: SR rises from 25.4/18.3 (instruction only) to 43.4/32.0 (all QAs, seen/unseen). An RL-tuned questioner does even better with far fewer questions: 47.8/33.6 SR at 0.71 questions per task versus 3.24 for All QAs, so knowing when and what to ask matters more than asking everything. The perturbed-oracle ablation (Table II) shows three things. Location answers are the most useful: withholding 50% of them drops unseen SR the most (33.6→32.2). The RL questioner adapts to a deficient oracle, asking 28% fewer location and 81% more direction questions, so its SR drop is smaller than the random questioner's (28.4→26.0). The timing ablation (Table III) shows that asking every step gives only a small gain (34.7 unseen SR) at a huge cost (21.39 questions per task). A heuristic questioner that asks when the performer is confused, given a random QA, does well on seen scenes (46.6) but generalizes poorly to unseen ones (29.5).
method: Dataset augmentation of ALFRED: original sub-goals are split (e.g. clean → put in sink / turn on faucet / turn off faucet) and merged (e.g. go to fridge + open fridge), giving 25 sub-goal task types. There are 34,253 training tasks, 1,296 valid-seen and 1,363 valid-unseen. Templated instructions often describe only the main action (e.g. 'Open the microwave' for goto+open), so the agent must reason about its own state.

Hybrid data collection on AMT: Turkers watch the pre-task scene clip and pick or type a question from templates (Location 'where is o?', Appearance 'what does o look like?', Direction 'which direction should I turn to?'). They then watch the expert demo, answer their own question and mark whether it was necessary. This covers 29,376 sub-goals with 2 annotators each, about 53K QAs, cost about $10K, Fleiss' κ=0.13.

Oracle answerer: templated answers built from AI2-THOR ground-truth state. Location gives the direction relative to the agent plus the containing receptacle. Appearance gives a color, mapped from pixel RGB, and a material from metadata. Direction compares the agent's end pose in the expert trajectory with its start pose.

Questioner: an LSTM seq2seq encoder-decoder with dot-product (Luong) attention. It encodes the instruction tokens, and the decoder is conditioned on the ResNet image feature. It emits a 2-token question (type ∈ {loc, app, dir} + target object) or a 'none' token. It is pre-trained on the questions Turkers selected in the training split.

Performer: an Episodic Transformer that encodes the full history of the instruction plus QAs, the egocentric frames and past actions. It is trained by imitation (cross-entropy against expert actions) on the training split with all combinations of question types and answers, and kept frozen during questioner RL.

RL fine-tuning of the questioner: actor-critic, where the action space is question type × object. Rewards are +1.0 for task success, −0.01 per step, −0.05 per question and −0.1 per invalid question. Fine-tuning is done on the valid-seen split. Variants are 'RL begin' (ask only at the start) and 'RL anytime' (may ask again after every 5 performer steps).

Model-confusion heuristic questioner (after Just Ask): the agent asks when min_t of (top-1 − top-2 action probability) < ε=0.5 over the action sequence. It is used as the 'Random MC' baseline and the 'RL anytime (MC)' timing variant.

setting.backbone: LSTM seq2seq questioner with ResNet image features (pre-trained on human QA choices, RL fine-tuned) + Episodic Transformer performer (trained by imitation learning, frozen during RL)
setting.training_data: The DialFRED training split: 34,253 sub-goal tasks augmented from ALFRED expert demonstrations, with templated instructions and all combinations of oracle QAs, used for performer imitation learning. About 53K human-annotated QAs over 29,376 sub-goals are used to pre-train the questioner. RL fine-tuning of the questioner uses oracle answers on the valid-seen split.
setting.observation: egocentric RGB (first-person frames) + natural-language instruction + question/answer text
setting.action_space: ALFRED discrete actions (5 navigation actions, e.g. Turn Left, plus 7 manipulation actions, e.g. Pickup/Slice) plus question actions (question type × target object, or none)
setting.privileged: Oracle answers are generated from ground-truth simulator state: object positions, receptacles, material metadata and the expert trajectory's end location. This is part of the benchmark protocol; the agent itself sees only RGB and text.

numbers_note: Results are sub-goal-level success rates on DialFRED's own augmented tasks, not ALFRED full-task SR/GC. PWSR is path-length-weighted SR measured in steps, and NQ is the number of questions per task. The RL questioner is fine-tuned on valid-seen, so valid-seen numbers for the RL variants are not held-out. Table II's 'Random' row (28.4 / 17.3 unseen) differs slightly from Table I's 'Random QA' row (27.9 / 17.3). Other rows not listed here: All QAs 43.4/32.0 SR, Random MC 46.6/29.5, RL anytime (Fixed 10) 46.3/32.4, and RL anytime (MC) 47.1/33.0 with NQ 0.31.
results: The RL-fine-tuned 'RL anytime' questioner-performer reaches 47.8 / 33.6 SR (seen/unseen) and 34.2 / 20.4 PWSR with 0.71 questions per task. This compares with 25.4 / 18.3 SR for the instruction-only performer. It also beats giving all valid QAs up front (43.4 / 32.0 SR with 3.24 questions) and random or confusion-triggered QA baselines. Allowing a question after every step gives the best numbers (51.9 / 34.7 SR), but at 21.39 questions per task.
limitations: The simulated user is a templated oracle that reads ground-truth simulator state, and questions are restricted to 3 template types × an object token, far from free-form human dialogue.

The questioner is RL-fine-tuned on the valid-seen split while the performer stays frozen. Absolute success on unseen scenes remains low (about 33.6% SR), and tasks are single sub-goals rather than full long-horizon ALFRED tasks.
Human question choices show low inter-annotator agreement (Fleiss' κ=0.13), which weakens the human-imitation signal used to pre-train the questioner.
